book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 8 · Vascular Access and Medication Administration
title: Starting an IV: Fluids, Technique and Complications
next: Chapter 8, Lesson 2: Giving medications safely, routes, and dose and drip math

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you had no IV access: you treated shock with bleeding control, positioning, warmth, oxygen and fast transport. Now, as a PCP:

  1. Choose the right fluid, catheter and drip set
  2. Start and maintain a line following the BC IV procedure
  3. Recognize and manage IV complications that never mattered to you before

Textbook: Chapter 8, PDF pages 549–621
slides.say: Welcome back. Vascular access is the biggest new skill you gain as a PCP. As an EMR, you had no IV access. When a patient was in shock, you controlled the bleeding, laid them flat, kept them warm, gave oxygen, and drove. That still matters. But now you can also put a catheter into a vein, which is what IV, or intravenous, means, and give fluid and drugs straight into the blood. That's powerful, and invasive, so it brings new risks. Today: choosing the fluid and equipment, starting and maintaining the line the BC way, and spotting complications early.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。血管通路是你升为 PCP 后最大的一项新技能。作为 EMR，你没有静脉通路权限。病人休克时，你止血、让他平躺、保暖、给氧、快速转运。这些依然重要。但现在你还可以把导管放进静脉，这就是 IV（静脉）的意思，把液体和药物直接送进血液。这很有力量，也是有创操作，所以带来新的风险。今天讲：怎样选液体和器材；怎样按 BC 的方式建立和维护静脉通路；以及怎样及早发现并发症。

slides.title: Why start an IV?
slides.body:
Two jobs: replace volume and give drugs

  • BC: replace fluid lost to hypovolemia or burns
  • BC: give medications
  • The book describes arm and hand veins, the external jugular vein, and IO
  • BC exam: IV access only; IO is BCEHS added scope
  • The IV is a tool: it never replaces fast transport
slides.say: Why start an IV at all? The BC IV procedure gives two reasons. First, to replace fluid and electrolytes, the salts in the blood, when a patient has lost volume, as in hypovolemia or a large burn. Second, to give medications. The textbook describes three ways in: veins of the hand and arm, the external jugular vein in the neck, and the intraosseous route, a needle into the bone marrow. Please note: the BC exam guidelines describe only IV access, with no procedure for starting an IO, so for your exam, a peripheral IV is your route. BCEHS PCPs may start an IO after added-scope training. And remember, the IV is a tool. It's never more important than getting the patient to hospital.
slides.sayZh: 为什么要开静脉？BC 的 IV 操作规程给了两个理由。第一，病人丢失了容量时补充液体和电解质（也就是血里的盐分），比如低血容量或大面积烧伤。第二，给药。教材讲了三条路：手和手臂的静脉、颈部的颈外静脉，以及骨髓腔途径，也就是把针打进骨髓。请注意：BC 考纲只讲静脉（IV）通路，没有开 IO 的操作规程，所以考试时，外周静脉是你的通路。BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1）培训后可以开 IO。还要记住，IV 只是工具，它永远没有把病人送到医院重要。

slides.title: Choosing the fluid: tonicity
slides.body:
Isotonicnormal saline, lactated Ringer'sadds volume, cells unchanged
HypotonicD5W once in the bodywater moves into cells
Hypertonic3% saline, albuminpulls water into vessels

Prehospital you will almost always hang normal saline or LR. D5W can raise pressure in the brain: avoid it in stroke and head injury.
slides.say: IV fluids are grouped by tonicity, which means whether a fluid makes water move into or out of cells. Isotonic fluids, like normal saline and lactated Ringer's, match the blood, so they add volume without making cells swell or shrink. That's what a patient who has lost volume needs. Hypotonic fluids let water move into the cells. D5W, five percent dextrose in water, is a trick question: it's isotonic in the bag, but the body uses up the sugar quickly and it becomes hypotonic. That can swell brain cells, so avoid it in stroke and head injury. Hypertonic fluids pull water into the vessels, but they're rarely used on emergency calls.
slides.sayZh: 静脉液体按张力分类，张力指的是液体会让水进入细胞还是离开细胞。等张液，比如生理盐水和乳酸林格液，和血液相当，能补充容量，又不会让细胞肿胀或皱缩，这正是丢失容量的病人需要的。低张液会让水进入细胞。D5W，也就是 5% 葡萄糖水，是个陷阱：在袋子里是等张的，但进入体内后葡萄糖很快被用掉，就变成低张液，可能让脑细胞肿胀，所以卒中和颅脑外伤要避免。高张液把水拉进血管，但急救出车时很少用。

slides.title: Saline is not blood
slides.body:
• Crystalloid carries no oxygen
  • About two-thirds leaves the vessels within an hour → 3:1 rule
  • Forcing BP back to normal dilutes blood and can disrupt clots
  • Book: boluses of 10–20 mL/kg, aiming for a radial pulse and clear mind
  • BC: 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing every 500 mL
slides.say: Every new PCP must own this idea: saline is not blood. Saline is a crystalloid, a salt-water fluid, and it carries no oxygen. About two-thirds of it leaves the vessels within an hour. That's why the book teaches the three-to-one rule: roughly three millilitres of crystalloid to replace one millilitre of lost blood. Yet more is not better. Push the blood pressure back to normal, and you dilute the blood and may break up clots that hold back internal bleeding. The book suggests ten to twenty millilitres per kilogram, aiming for a radial pulse and a clear mind. For BC, use the protocol: twenty per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred.
slides.sayZh: 每个新 PCP 都必须牢记：生理盐水不是血。生理盐水是晶体液，也就是盐水类液体，它不带氧。大约三分之二会在一小时内离开血管。所以书里讲 3:1 原则：大约三毫升晶体液才能补回一毫升丢失的血。但并不是越多越好。把血压硬推回正常，会稀释血液，还可能冲开正在压住内出血的血凝块。书里建议每公斤十到二十毫升，目标是摸得到桡动脉、神志清楚。BC 按流程来：每公斤二十毫升，最多两升，每五百毫升复评一次。

slides.title: Your equipment: sets and catheters
slides.body:
ItemSizeUse
Macrodrip set10 or 15 gtt/mLvolume replacement
Microdrip set60 gtt/mLdrugs, children
Catheter14–16 Gfluid; possible blood or surgery
Catheter18–20 Gadults who don't need fluid
Catheter20–26 Gchildren, by age

Smaller gauge number = bigger catheter = faster flow.
slides.say: Now your equipment. Every drip set shows its drop factor, the number of drops that make one millilitre. A macrodrip set gives ten or fifteen big drops per millilitre, for replacing volume. A microdrip set gives sixty tiny drops per millilitre, for medications and children, where you need tight control. Catheters are sized by gauge, and the numbers run backwards: the smaller the number, the bigger the catheter. Fourteen or sixteen gauge is for a patient who needs fluid, or may need blood or surgery. Eighteen or twenty gauge suits most adults who don't need fluid. Children get twenty to twenty-six gauge, depending on age.
slides.sayZh: 再看器材。每个输液器都标着滴系数，就是多少滴等于一毫升。大滴输液器每毫升十滴或十五滴，滴子大，用来补充容量。微滴输液器每毫升六十滴，滴子很小，用于给药和儿童，需要精确控制的时候用。留置针按号数（G）分大小，而且是反着来的：数字越小，导管越粗。十四或十六号给需要补液、或可能要输血或手术的病人；十八或二十号适合大多数不需要补液的成人；儿童按年龄用二十到二十六号。

slides.q: A 60-year-old man is hypotensive after vomiting blood for an hour. You plan to give fluid en route. Which setup fits best?
options: 22 G in the hand with a 60-drop set
14 or 16 G in the antecubital vein with a 10-drop set
20 G at the wrist with a 60-drop set
24 G in the forearm with a 15-drop set
slides.say: Quiz time. A sixty-year-old man is hypotensive after vomiting blood for an hour, and you plan to give fluid on the way to hospital. Which setup fits best? A, a twenty-two gauge in the hand with a sixty-drop set. B, a fourteen or sixteen gauge in the antecubital vein, inside the elbow, with a ten-drop set. C, a twenty gauge at the wrist with a sixty-drop set. D, a twenty-four gauge in the forearm with a fifteen-drop set. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 测验时间。一名六十岁男性呕血一小时后低血压，你打算在去医院的路上补液。哪种配置最合适？A，手背二十二号针，配六十滴输液器。B，肘前静脉（肘窝内侧）十四或十六号针，配十滴输液器。C，手腕处二十号针，配六十滴输液器。D，前臂二十四号针，配十五滴输液器。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A patient who needs volume gets a large catheter, fourteen or sixteen gauge, in a big vein like the antecubital, which the book recommends for unstable patients, plus a macrodrip set for fast flow. A and C use a microdrip set, which is built for slow, precise drug delivery, and smaller catheters. D's twenty-four gauge is a child-size catheter, far too small to move fluid quickly.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。需要补容量的病人要用粗导管，十四或十六号，放在像肘前这样的大静脉里（书里推荐不稳定病人用肘前静脉），再配大滴输液器，流速才快。A 和 C 用的是微滴输液器，是为慢速、精确给药设计的，导管也偏细。D 的二十四号是儿童尺寸的导管，太细，没法快速补液。

slides.title: Picking the vein
slides.body:
• Straight, springy vein; avoid valves and joints
  • Start distal, then work up the arm
  • Unstable or needs fluid fast: use the antecubital vein
  • Avoid: swollen limb, dialysis fistula, mastectomy side, injured limb
  • Not just below an open wound; leg veins raise clot risk
  • BC stroke: en route, 18 G above the wrist, right side preferred
slides.say: Choosing the vein is half the success. Look for a straight, springy vein, and avoid valves, which feel like small bumps, and joints. Normally you start low on the arm and work upward, so a failed site still leaves room above it. But if the patient is unstable or needs fluid fast, go straight to the antecubital vein, inside the elbow. Avoid a swollen arm, an arm with a dialysis fistula, the side of a past mastectomy, and any injured or infected limb. Leg veins carry a higher risk of clots. For stroke, BC is specific: en route, an eighteen gauge above the wrist, preferably on the right side.
slides.sayZh: 选对静脉就成功了一半。找又直又有弹性的静脉，避开静脉瓣（摸起来像小鼓包）和关节。通常从手臂远端开始，再往上走，这样一个部位失败了，上方还有位置可用。但如果病人不稳定或需要快速补液，直接用肘前静脉，也就是肘窝内侧。避开肿胀的手臂、有透析瘘管的手臂、做过乳房切除的那一侧，以及任何受伤或感染的肢体。下肢静脉形成血栓的风险更高。卒中病人 BC 有具体规定：转运途中，在手腕以上用十八号针，最好在右侧。

slides.title: The BC IV procedure
slides.body:
1. Keep aseptic technique throughout
  2. Inspect catheter, fluid and set; prime the tubing
  3. Choose and prepare the site, then start the IV
  4. Connect the tubing and infuse
  5. Calculate and maintain the flow rate
  6. Secure the IV

Then maintain it: reassess ABCs, vitals and the IV site, tubing and bag every 5–15 minutes.
slides.say: Here's the BC IV procedure, the sequence examiners expect. Keep aseptic technique, meaning everything stays as clean as possible, the whole way through. Inspect the catheter, the fluid bag and the drip set, then prime the tubing, which means running fluid through it to push out all the air. Choose and prepare the site, and start the IV. Connect the tubing and let the fluid run. Calculate and maintain the right flow rate; we'll practise that math next lesson. Then secure the line. And the job continues: BC asks you to reassess the ABCs, the vital signs, and the IV itself every five to fifteen minutes.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的 IV 操作规程，也是考官希望看到的顺序。全程保持无菌技术，也就是一切尽量保持干净。检查留置针、液体袋和输液器，然后排气，就是让液体流过管路，把空气全部排出去。选好并准备穿刺部位，建立静脉通路。接上输液管，让液体流起来。计算并维持正确的滴速，这部分的计算下节课练。然后固定好管路。工作还没完：BC 要求每五到十五分钟复评一次 ABC、生命体征，以及静脉通路本身。

slides.title: Hands on: placing the catheter
slides.body:
Band 15–25 cm above→Bevel up, about 45°→Flash: drop to about 15°→Slide catheter in
  • Press above the tip, remove needle, sharps container at once
  • Connect, release the band, open the line, watch for swelling
  • Loop the tubing; never tape all the way round a limb
  • Never pull the catheter back over the needle
  • Two misses? Let your partner try
slides.say: Let's walk through the insertion. Tie the constricting band, a tourniquet just tight enough to fill the veins, about fifteen to twenty-five centimetres above your site. Clean the skin, pull it tight so the vein can't roll, and go in bevel up at about forty-five degrees. When you see a flash of blood, drop to about fifteen degrees, advance a little more, then slide the catheter off the needle into the vein. Press on the vein above the tip, remove the needle, and drop it straight into the sharps container. Connect, release the band, and watch for swelling. And never pull a catheter back over its needle: the needle can slice it off.
slides.sayZh: 我们走一遍穿刺过程。在穿刺点上方大约十五到二十五厘米扎上止血带，松紧以让静脉充盈为准。消毒皮肤，把皮肤绷紧让静脉不滚动，针尖斜面朝上，大约四十五度进针。看到回血后，把角度降到大约十五度，再往前推进一点，然后把导管从针上推进静脉里。按住导管尖端上方的静脉，退出针芯，立刻丢进锐器盒。接上输液管，松开止血带，观察有没有肿胀。还有，绝不能把导管往回套到针上，针会把导管割断。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: where the IV appears
slides.body:
BC protocols: EMRs have no IV access. The PCP adds it, often en route.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Hypovolemia: stop bleeding, supine, warm, O₂
  • Diabetic: oral glucose; EMR glucagon if mentation is poor
  • Opioid overdose: ventilate, naloxone
  • Stroke: glucose check, FAST-VAN, timely transport

PCP adds

  • Hypovolemia: IV en route or if delayed; 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Diabetic: IV D10W 10–25 g; glucagon only if no IV
  • Overdose: IV naloxone if still unconscious and apneic
  • Stroke: 18 G en route; chest pain: IV with running fluid
  • Head injury: IV TKVO if systolic > 120
slides.say: This slide shows how your role changes across the BC protocols. On the left is what every licence level does. For hypovolemia: stop the bleeding, lay the patient flat, keep them warm, give oxygen. For a diabetic emergency: oral glucose, or glucagon from an EMR when the patient can't protect the airway. For an opioid overdose: ventilate and give naloxone. On the right is what the PCP adds, and it's almost always the IV. In hypovolemia, a line and fluid en route or during a delay. For low blood sugar, D10W, ten percent dextrose, through the IV, with glucagon only if you can't get a line. Stroke, chest pain and head injury each have their own IV rule.
slides.sayZh: 这张幻灯片显示你的角色在 BC 各流程里怎么变化。左栏是所有级别都做的：低血容量：止血、平卧、保暖、给氧。糖尿病急症：口服葡萄糖；病人无法保护气道时，EMR 给胰高血糖素。阿片类过量：通气并给纳洛酮。右栏是 PCP 增加的，几乎全是静脉通路。低血容量时，在转运途中或有延误时开静脉并补液。低血糖时，经静脉给 D10W（10% 葡萄糖），只有开不了静脉才用胰高血糖素。卒中、胸痛和颅脑外伤也各有自己的静脉规定。

slides.title: Trouble at the IV site
slides.body:
ProblemClueAction
Infiltrationswollen, tight, sore; still drips with vein pressed abovestop, remove, new site
Occlusiondrip slows, blood in tubingdraw back gently; never push
Hematomablood pooling at the sitedirect pressure
Arterial puncturebright red, spurting bloodremove, press ≥ 5 min
Nerve injurysudden shooting pain, then numbremove, new site

Slow drip? First check the band, kinks, bag height and cold fluid.
slides.say: Now the local problems at the IV site. Infiltration means fluid is leaking into the tissue instead of the vein. The site swells and feels tight and sore, and fluid keeps dripping even when you press on the vein above. Stop, remove the catheter, and start again elsewhere. If the drip slows or blood backs up in the tubing, think occlusion, a blockage. Draw back gently with a syringe, but never push a clot into the patient. Bright red, spurting blood means an artery: pull out and press for at least five minutes. A sudden shooting pain means a nerve: remove it.
slides.sayZh: 再说穿刺部位的局部问题。渗漏是指液体漏进了组织而不是静脉里：局部肿胀、发紧、疼痛，就算按住上方的静脉，液体还在滴。停止输液，拔管，换个地方重来。如果滴速变慢或血倒流进管路，要想到堵塞。可以用注射器轻轻往回抽，但绝不能把血块推进病人体内。鲜红、喷射状的血说明扎到了动脉：拔出并按压至少五分钟。突然一阵放射性剧痛说明碰到了神经：立即拔管。

slides.title: Systemic complications
slides.body:
ProblemClueAction
Circulatory overloaddyspnea, crackles, JVD, high BPslow to KVO, sit up, O₂
Air embolismsudden distress, unequal breath sounds, cyanosis on O₂left side, head down, 100% O₂
Catheter shearpiece of catheter lostleft side, head up, legs down
Pyrogenic reactionfever, chills, backache within 30 minstop; new line in the other arm
Allergic reactionitch, hives, wheezestop the fluid, keep the catheter

If the line works, keep it: you may need it for treatment.
slides.say: Systemic complications affect the whole body, and some can kill. Circulatory overload means too much fluid: shortness of breath, crackles in the lungs, distended neck veins and high blood pressure. Slow the line to keep the vein open, sit the patient up, and give oxygen. An air embolism causes sudden breathing distress, unequal breath sounds, and blue skin even on oxygen. Turn the patient onto the left side, head down, to trap the air in the heart, and give one hundred percent oxygen. For a sheared catheter, also the left side, but head up. Notice the rule at the bottom: with systemic problems, you keep a working line.
slides.sayZh: 全身性并发症影响整个身体，有的会致命。循环超负荷就是液体太多：气短、肺部湿啰音、颈静脉怒张、血压升高。把滴速调到维持静脉开放，让病人坐起来，给氧。空气栓塞表现为突然呼吸窘迫、两侧呼吸音不等、吸着氧仍然发绀。让病人左侧卧、头低位，把空气困在心脏里，并给百分之百的氧。导管断裂也是左侧卧，但要头高位。注意底部这条规则：出现全身性问题时，保留还能用的静脉通路。

slides.q: You're giving fluid to a hypotensive 82-year-old with a history of heart failure. She becomes more short of breath, with crackles and distended neck veins. What should you do?
options: Speed up the fluid, since she is getting worse
Remove the IV catheter right away
Slow the IV to keep the vein open, sit her up, give oxygen, reassess
Turn her onto her left side with her head down
slides.say: Second question. You're giving fluid to a hypotensive eighty-two-year-old with a history of heart failure. She becomes more short of breath, and you hear crackles and see distended neck veins. What should you do? A, speed up the fluid, since she is getting worse. B, remove the IV catheter right away. C, slow the IV to keep the vein open, sit her up, give oxygen, and reassess. D, turn her onto her left side with her head down. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 第二题。你在给一位有心衰病史、低血压的八十二岁女性补液。她越来越气短，你听到湿啰音，看到颈静脉怒张。你该怎么做？A，加快补液，因为她在变差。B，立刻拔掉留置针。C，把滴速调到维持静脉开放，让她坐起来，给氧，复评。D，让她左侧卧、头低位。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. These are classic signs of circulatory overload, and older patients with heart disease are at high risk. Slow the rate, sit her up and support her breathing. A would make the overload worse. B throws away a working line you may need; with systemic complications you keep a patent IV. D is the position for an air embolism, not fluid overload. For older patients, the book advises small boluses of two to three hundred millilitres, listening to the lungs before and after each one.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。这些是循环超负荷的典型表现，有心脏病的老人风险很高。减慢滴速，让她坐起来，支持呼吸。A 会让超负荷更严重。B 扔掉了一条你可能还需要的通路，出现全身性并发症时要保留通畅的静脉通路。D 是空气栓塞的体位，不是液体超负荷的。对老年病人，书里建议每次小剂量推注两到三百毫升，每次前后都听一听肺部。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Never delay transport for an IV: many BC protocols say en route
  • Reassess the patient and the IV every 5–15 minutes
  • After the first flush, turn the rate back down
  • Change the bag at about 50 mL; never let the drip chamber run dry
  • Elderly or heart, lung, kidney disease: small boluses, listen to lungs
  • Document gauge, site, attempts, fluid and rate
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch for. First, never delay transport to start a line; the BC hypovolemia, stroke, chest and abdominal trauma protocols all put the IV en route. Second, every five to fifteen minutes you now reassess two things: the patient, and the IV site, tubing and bag. Third, after you flush a new line wide open, turn it back down. Forgetting is the most common prehospital cause of fluid overload. Fourth, change the bag with about fifty millilitres left, and never let the drip chamber run dry, or air can enter the vein. Fifth, go gently with older and heart patients. And document the gauge, site, attempts, fluid and rate.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你需要新注意的。第一，绝不为开静脉耽误转运；BC 的低血容量、卒中、胸部和腹部创伤流程都把开静脉放在转运途中。第二，你现在每五到十五分钟要复评两样东西：病人，以及静脉的穿刺点、管路和液体袋。第三，新管路冲管时开到最大，冲完一定要把滴速调回来。忘记调回是院前液体超负荷最常见的原因。第四，袋里剩大约五十毫升就换袋，绝不能让滴壶流空，否则空气可能进入静脉。第五，对老人和心脏病人补液要温和。还要记录针号、部位、尝试次数、液体和滴速。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. IV access is new for the PCP: volume and drugs; IO isn't on the BC exam
  2. Big catheter and macrodrip for volume; follow the BC IV procedure
  3. Watch site and patient; systemic problem? Keep the line

Next: giving medications safely, routes, and dose and drip math
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: IV access is new for you as a PCP. You use it to replace volume in hypovolemia and burns, and to give drugs. The BC exam describes only IV access; IO comes with BCEHS added-scope training. Two: for volume, choose a big catheter and a macrodrip set, follow the BC IV procedure, and reassess every five to fifteen minutes. Three: watch the site and the whole patient, and with systemic problems, keep the working line. Next lesson, we'll use this line to give medications, and practise the dose and drip math. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，静脉通路是你作为 PCP 新获得的技能，用来在低血容量和烧伤时补充容量，以及给药。BC 执照考试只讲静脉通路；IO 属于 BCEHS 扩展范围（Schedule 1 培训后）。二，补容量要用粗导管和大滴输液器，按 BC 的 IV 规程做，每五到十五分钟复评一次。三，既要盯住穿刺部位，也要看整个病人；出现全身性问题时，保留还能用的通路。下节课我们用这条通路给药，并练习剂量和滴速计算。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
